    Introduction to Jupyter Notebooks on Sagehen

    Welcome!

    This workshop teaches you how to use Jupyter Notebooks for interactive Python development on the Sagehen HPC cluster. Jupyter Notebooks combine executable code, text explanations, and visualizations in a single document, making them ideal for exploratory analysis, teaching, and scientific computing.

    Why take this workshop?

    Jupyter Notebooks are powerful tools for computational research, and when combined with the resources of an HPC cluster, they become even more valuable. After this workshop, you will be able to:

    • Understand what Jupyter Notebooks are and why they’re useful for research
    • Launch Jupyter on Sagehen using the OnDemand portal
    • Work with different cell types (code, markdown) and understand the notebook execution model
    • Write Python code that explores data and produces visualizations
    • Manage Python environments and install packages for your notebooks
    • Apply best practices for reproducible and shareable notebooks
    • Convert notebooks to different formats and automate analyses
    Prerequisite

    What you’ll need

    • Your Pomona College account with HPC access
    • A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge)
    • Access to the Sagehen cluster (sagehen.hpc.pomona.edu)
    • Basic Python knowledge (variables, functions, simple data structures)
    • 30-40 minutes for the full workshop

    If you’re new to Python, we recommend learning Python basics first. This workshop assumes you can write simple Python statements.

    Workshop structure

    This workshop is organized as follows:

    Episode Time Topic
    1 15 min + 5 ex What Are Jupyter Notebooks? — history, use cases, and why notebooks on HPC
    2 15 min + 10 ex Launching Jupyter on Sagehen via the OnDemand portal with proper resource requests
    3 15 min + 10 ex Notebook interface basics — JupyterLab layout, file browser, and the kernel model
    4 20 min + 15 ex Working with cells — code vs. markdown, execution order, and editing shortcuts
    5 20 min + 10 ex Python fundamentals in notebooks — imports, variables, control flow
    6 25 min + 20 ex Data analysis in notebooks — loading, exploring, and summarising data
    7 15 min + 10 ex Visualization in notebooks — matplotlib basics and inline figures
    8 20 min + 15 ex Managing kernels and environments — conda envs and custom kernels for Jupyter
    9 15 min + 10 ex Sharing and exporting — HTML, PDF, .py, and integrating with version control
    10 15 min + 10 ex Best practices for reproducible, shareable notebooks

    Total teaching time: ~5 hours (175 minutes teaching + 115 minutes exercises, plus breaks)

    Key technologies

    This workshop focuses on tools available on Sagehen:

    • JupyterLab - Interactive notebook environment (modern Jupyter interface)
    • Python 3 - Programming language (via conda)
    • conda - Environment and package management
    • Sagehen HPC cluster - Computing resources with module system
    • OnDemand portal - Web interface for cluster access (https://ondemand.hpc.pomona.edu/)

    Learning outcomes

    By the end of this workshop, you will be able to:

    • Explain what Jupyter Notebooks are and their advantages for computational research
    • Launch JupyterLab on Sagehen with appropriate resource requests
    • Create and execute notebook cells with proper output handling
    • Write Python code that loads, processes, and visualizes data
    • Create and switch between Python environments
    • Manage dependencies reproducibly using environment files
    • Export notebooks to HTML, PDF, or Python scripts
    • Apply version control best practices to notebook-based workflows
    Callout

    Getting help

    If you encounter issues during the workshop: - Email: its-hpc@pomona.edu (most reliable) - Slack: #hpc-help channel (Pomona CS Slack workspace) - Office hours: See ITS-HPC website for Andrew Wilson’s availability - Troubleshooting: Check the Reference section for common issues

    Before you begin

    Please complete the following before the workshop:

    1. Verify HPC access: Try logging into https://ondemand.hpc.pomona.edu/ - if it works, you’re ready
    2. Check browser compatibility: We support modern Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge
    3. Test internet connection: Jupyter requires a persistent network connection
    4. Optional: Create a work directory: ssh sagehen && mkdir -p ~/jupyter-workshop

    Ready to get started? Let’s dive in!

    Questions or suggestions? Please contact its-hpc@pomona.edu or open an issue on our GitHub repository.

    What You Need

    Before the workshop, please verify the following:

    1. Pomona College HPC Account

    You need an active HPC account on the Sagehen cluster.

    Callout

    Verify your account

    1. Go to https://ondemand.hpc.pomona.edu/
    2. Log in with your Pomona College username and password
    3. Complete DUO authentication on your phone
    4. If you see the OnDemand dashboard, you’re ready!

    If you can’t log in: - Verify your Pomona username (ask ITS Help Desk if unsure) - Ensure DUO is registered (register at https://duo.pomona.edu/) - Contact its-hpc@pomona.edu for account issues

    2. Web Browser

    You’ll use your web browser to access JupyterLab. Ensure you have a modern browser:

    • Google Chrome (recommended)
    • Firefox (recommended)
    • Safari (Mac)
    • Microsoft Edge (Windows)

    Avoid very old versions of Internet Explorer.

    3. Internet Connection

    Jupyter requires a persistent network connection to the cluster. Ensure:

    • Stable WiFi or wired connection
    • If on campus WiFi, make sure you’re on “Pomona” network (not “Guest”)
    • Off-campus? VPN may be required (check with ITS Help Desk)

    4. Basic Python Knowledge

    This workshop assumes you know:

    • Variables and data types (strings, numbers, lists)
    • Simple functions and for loops
    • How to read and understand error messages

    If you’re new to Python, we recommend completing a Python basics tutorial first. Good resources:

    Callout

    Python Learning Resources

    • Codecademy Python Course (interactive, free): https://www.codecademy.com/learn/learn-python-3
    • Python for Everybody (comprehensive, free): https://www.py4e.com/
    • Kaggle Python Micro-Courses (bite-sized, free): https://www.kaggle.com/learn/python

    All assume no prior experience. Complete any of these and you’ll be ready!

    Pre-Workshop Checklist

    Before the workshop, complete these steps:

    If all items are checked, you’re ready for the workshop!

    Optional: Pre-Workshop Learning

    If you want to get ahead:

    1. Learn basic Python (if new to programming)
      • Complete 1-2 hours of Python basics
      • Understand variables, loops, functions
    2. Explore pandas DataFrames (data analysis library)
      • DataFrames are like spreadsheets in Python
      • Used heavily in our examples
      • (But we’ll teach this during the workshop, so it’s optional)
    3. Browse Jupyter documentation
      • Visit https://jupyter.org/ to see what Jupyter is
      • Watch a 5-minute “Jupyter Notebook tutorial” video on YouTube
      • (We’ll cover everything in the workshop, so this is just for context)

    Workshop Materials

    The workshop provides:

    • 6 interactive episodes covering Jupyter from basics to best practices
    • Code examples you can run in JupyterLab on Sagehen
    • Hands-on exercises to practice what you learn
    • Reference guide with common commands and troubleshooting

    All materials are available through the workshop website (you’re reading it now!).

    Getting Help Before the Workshop

    If you encounter issues:

    Can’t access OnDemand: - Email: its-hpc@pomona.edu - Subject: “Can’t access OnDemand” - Include: your Pomona username, error message (if any)

    Trouble with DUO: - Contact ITS Help Desk: (909) 621-8061 - Or: https://www.pomona.edu/its/ - They handle DUO issues

    Browser problems: - Try a different browser (Chrome, Firefox) - Clear browser cache (Ctrl+Shift+Delete / Cmd+Shift+Delete) - Try in incognito/private mode

    Internet connectivity: - Try on campus WiFi or wired connection - Off-campus? Contact ITS about VPN access

    Python knowledge gaps: - Check resources above for 1-2 hours of learning - Basic Python is essential; reach out if you need guidance

    Troubleshooting Sagehen Access

    If you can’t access OnDemand:

    Check 1: Is OnDemand the right URL? - Correct: https://ondemand.hpc.pomona.edu/ - Wrong: ondemand.hpc.pomona.com (no “https”)

    Check 2: Are you using the right username? - Pomona username (what you use for email) - Not your full name - Not “student” or generic names

    Check 3: Is DUO working? - Check your phone: Is DUO app installed and current? - Is your device registered at https://duo.pomona.edu/? - Try “Call me instead of code” if codes don’t work

    Check 4: Is the cluster working? - Check cluster status: its-hpc@pomona.edu - Rarely, Sagehen goes down for maintenance - Status posted on cluster website

    Still stuck? - Email: its-hpc@pomona.edu - Include: - Your Pomona username - Exact error message (copy-paste) - What you’ve already tried - Preferred contact method and time

    What Happens During the Workshop

    The workshop is hands-on and interactive:

    1. First episode: Lecture + discussion about Jupyter (15 min) + small exercise
    2. Subsequent episodes: Lecture (20-40 min) + guided exercises (15-25 min)
    3. Each exercise: You write code in JupyterLab on Sagehen and see results immediately
    4. Challenges: Optional deeper exercises for those who want more challenge

    You’ll need: - A web browser open to OnDemand - JupyterLab launched (we’ll do this in Episode 2) - Time to type and think

    Questions?

    Reach out anytime:

    • Email: its-hpc@pomona.edu
    • Slack: #hpc-help (Pomona CS Slack workspace)
    • Office Hours: See instructor availability on ITS-HPC website

    We’re here to help you succeed!
